key_insight: A variational quantum circuit can generate exact uniform permutations under hardware connectivity constraints, achieving linear depth on nearest-neighbor layouts.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical route to permutation-based quantum subroutines on realistic devices without requiring all-to-all qubit connectivity.
method: Build the circuit architecture from the device interaction graph.
Use controlled-SWAP-based unitary constructions and optimize variational parameters to match uniform permutation statistics.
Prove exact uniformity with quadratic circuit size and O(n) depth on linear nearest-neighbor topologies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact constructions and theoretical proofs, including a result that Beneš-like architectures remain non-uniform for any parameter choice.
watch_item: The approach appears exact but hardware realization will still depend on the cost and robustness of variational optimization under noisy devices.
paper_title: Variational Approach for Uniform Quantum Permutation Generators
